## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the determination of soil aggregate stability
using the wet sieving method. Aggregate stability quantifies the
resistance of soil structural units to disintegration when subjected to
disruptive forces such as wetting, raindrop impact, and mechanical
disturbance. It is a key indicator of soil physical quality, erosion
susceptibility, and the effects of management practices (tillage,
cover cropping, organic amendments) on soil structure
[@kemper1986; @nimmo2004].


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried mineral soil samples sieved to a defined
  aggregate size class (typically 1--2 mm or 2--4 mm). Samples must
  have been collected and processed per
  [SOP-F400 Soil Sampling](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd).
- **Does not apply to:** Sandy soils with negligible aggregation,
  organic soils (histosols), or aggregate characterization by dry
  sieving alone
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Sodium hexametaphosphate (dispersing agent) is a mild
  irritant. Hydrogen peroxide (if used for organic matter correction)
  is a strong oxidizer.
- **Physical:** Drying oven operates at 105 C; burn risk from hot
  containers.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling dispersing solution or H~2~O~2~)
- [ ] Heat-resistant gloves (when handling containers from the oven)

### Emergency Procedures

For chemical splashes, flush with water for at least 15 minutes. Refer
to [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

### Equipment

|:--------------------------------------|:----------|:-------------------------------|
| Wet sieving apparatus (Yoder-type or Eijkelkamp) | SGM 133 | Oscillating sieve holder |
| Nested sieves (e.g., 2 mm, 1 mm, 0.5 mm, 0.25 mm, 0.053 mm) | SGM 133 | Stainless steel, 8 cm diameter |

| Desiccator with active desiccant      | SGM 133   |                                |
| Pre-weighed aluminum drying tins      | SGM 133   |                                |

### Reagents and Consumables

| Item                                       | Notes                          |
|:-------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Deionized water                            | For wetting and sieving        |
| Sodium hexametaphosphate solution (5 g/L)  | For dispersing residual aggregates (sand correction) |
| Hydrogen peroxide (30%), optional          | For removing organic matter if sand correction requires it |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Sample Preparation

1. Air-dry soil samples at room temperature until friable (typically
   48--72 hours)
2. Gently break large clods along natural planes of weakness by hand;
   do not grind or crush
3. Dry-sieve the sample through a nest of sieves to isolate the
   desired aggregate size class (e.g., 1--2 mm or 2--4 mm)
4. Discard material outside the target size range for this analysis
5. Weigh out replicate subsamples (typically 4.0 g each, minimum 3
   replicates per sample) into labeled containers

### 6.2 Pre-Wetting (Capillary Wetting)

Rapid wetting causes slaking, which may overestimate instability for
some research questions. If slow pre-wetting is desired:

1. Place each subsample on a moistened filter paper in a closed
   container
2. Allow capillary wetting for 10 minutes (or a duration standardized
   for the study)
3. Proceed to wet sieving

If the goal is to assess slaking resistance under rapid wetting (the
more common approach), omit the pre-wetting step and place air-dried
aggregates directly onto the sieve.

### 6.3 Wet Sieving

1. Place the pre-weighed aggregates on the top sieve of the wet sieving
   apparatus (e.g., 0.25 mm for a single-sieve method, or the top of
   a nested stack)
2. Raise the water level in the sieving cans until the sieves are
   submerged to the appropriate depth (typically 1--2 cm above the
   sieve mesh)
3. Allow the aggregates to soak for 5 minutes (standardize this time
   for the study) before starting oscillation
4. Start the wet sieving apparatus. The standard cycle is 3 cm stroke
   at 34 cycles per minute for 3 minutes [@kemper1986]. Record the
   exact settings used.
5. After sieving, carefully raise the sieves from the water

### 6.4 Collection and Drying

1. Backwash the material retained on each sieve into a pre-weighed
   aluminum tin using a wash bottle with deionized water
2. Transfer any material that passed through the finest sieve (the
   material in the sieving can) into a separate tin if size
   fractionation is desired
3. Dry all tins at 105 C for 24 hours (or until constant mass)
4. Cool in a desiccator and weigh to the nearest 0.001 g

### 6.5 Sand Correction

The material retained on the sieve after wet sieving includes both
water-stable aggregates and primary sand particles that are inherently
larger than the sieve openings. To correct for sand:

1. Add 50 mL of 5 g/L sodium hexametaphosphate to the dried residue
   in each tin
2. Allow to soak for at least 2 hours (or overnight) to fully disperse
   remaining aggregates
3. Pour the dispersed slurry back through the same sieve used in the
   wet sieving step
4. Rinse thoroughly with deionized water
5. Backwash the retained sand into a clean tin, dry at 105 C, cool,
   and weigh

### 6.6 Calculations

**Water-stable aggregates (WSA) as a fraction of the total sample,
corrected for sand:**

$$
\text{WSA} (\%) = \frac{M_{\text{stable}} - M_{\text{sand}}}{M_{\text{total}} - M_{\text{sand}}} \times 100
$$

where:

- $M_{\text{stable}}$ = oven-dry mass of material retained on the sieve
  after wet sieving (g)
- $M_{\text{sand}}$ = oven-dry mass of sand retained after dispersal (g)
- $M_{\text{total}}$ = initial oven-dry equivalent mass of the
  subsample (g; corrected for moisture using gravimetric moisture from
  [SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd))

If a nested sieve set is used, calculate the mean weight diameter (MWD):

$$
\text{MWD} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \bar{x}_i \, w_i
$$

where $\bar{x}_i$ is the mean diameter of the $i$th size fraction and
$w_i$ is the proportion of the total sample weight in that fraction
(after sand correction) [@vanBavel1950].


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Run a minimum of 3 replicates per sample; report the mean and
  standard deviation
- The coefficient of variation among replicates should be less than 15%
- Include a laboratory reference soil in each batch to monitor method
  consistency over time
- Record all apparatus settings (stroke length, frequency, sieving
  duration) so results are reproducible
- *TBD -- identify or prepare a reference soil for long-term QC
  tracking*


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Sieved soil and sand          | Standard trash or return to sample stock |
| Sodium hexametaphosphate solution | Drain with copious water (non-hazardous at this concentration) |
| H~2~O~2~ waste (if used)     | Dilute and drain, or collect for EH&S    |
| Used aluminum tins            | Clean and reuse, or recycle              |

## 10. Training Record

Before performing this procedure independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Complete [SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)
   training (required for moisture correction)
4. Observe a trained operator perform the full procedure including
   sand correction
5. Perform the analysis under supervision with acceptable replicate
   precision (CV less than 15%)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
